topic: science corporation implants vision restoring chip
headline_marked: Science Corporation [[implants vision-restoring chip in first Stargardt patient]]
headline: Science Corporation implants vision-restoring chip in first Stargardt patient
summary: The PRIMA chip, already available in Europe for other conditions, offers hope for Stargardt disease, an inherited condition causing central vision loss. The first patient in a trial was able to read a word after the implant.
details: Science Corporation, led by Neuralink co-founder Max Hodak, has implanted its PRIMA vision-restoring chip into its first patient with Stargardt disease. This inherited eye condition gradually destroys central vision, affecting approximately 150,000 people worldwide. The patient, part of a trial in Australia, was able to see a letter and read a word during initial rehabilitation sessions.

Stargardt disease is currently considered incurable, making this development significant. It causes the gradual death of the eye's light-sensing cells in the outer retina, leading to a central blind spot while potentially sparing the inner retina that transmits signals to the brain.

The PRIMA device works by implanting a small 2x2mm chip in the back of the eye where photoreceptors have degenerated. Patients then wear camera-equipped glasses that transmit visual information to the chip, which acts as artificial photoreceptors, converting light into electrical signals for the optic nerve.

Currently, the implant provides a black-and-white, high-contrast, sharp patch of central vision, described as "looking through a straw" due to its small field of view. Science Corporation aims to develop larger implants and smaller electrodes in the next five years to achieve a wider field of view and closer to native acuity.

Beyond vision restoration, Science Corporation is pursuing a broader vision for brain-computer interfaces (BCIs), including applications for other neurodegenerative diseases and stroke. Their BCI sensor, unlike Neuralink's, is designed to rest on top of the brain inside the skull, rather than being inserted into brain tissue.

topic: rivian mind robotics hires doug field
headline_marked: [[Rivian's Mind Robotics hires former Ford EV chief Doug Field]] as president
headline: Rivian's Mind Robotics hires former Ford EV chief Doug Field as president
summary: Doug Field, a veteran leader from Ford's EV division, Apple, and Tesla, takes the helm as president of Mind Robotics, Rivian's secretive robotics partner founded by CEO RJ Scaringe.
details: Rivian CEO RJ Scaringe's partner startup, Mind Robotics, has appointed Doug Field as its new president. Field previously served as Ford's EV and software chief, and also held significant roles at Apple, including leading Project Titan, and as chief vehicle engineer at Tesla for the Model 3.

Mind Robotics, founded in 2025 by Scaringe, aims to build "universally capable robots" for use in Rivian's factories and other industrial applications. The secretive startup has already secured over $1 billion in financing.

Scaringe expressed excitement about Field joining, highlighting his track record of delivering new technologies and fostering strong teams. Field's leadership is expected to be crucial as Mind Robotics deploys robots into real factories.

Field's appointment comes at a pivotal time for robotics, marked by rapid advancements in physical AI alongside hardware and software development challenges. Mind Robotics has not yet revealed if its designs are humanoid or an alternative form factor.

While Scaringe intends to keep Mind Robotics separate from Rivian, the companies are closely linked. Mind Robotics leverages AI training data from Rivian, will test its robots in Rivian's factories, and Rivian holds equity in the startup as its first customer.

Field stated his enthusiasm for integrating AI and robotics, calling it a critical engineering challenge. He emphasized Mind's unique advantage of deploying and learning within a high-volume factory from day one, aiming to redefine manufacturing.
